references.text: Describes the 'tent of meeting' (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד) as the place where the Lord meets with the Israelites, a concept also used in Exodus 33:7
The Lord promises to meet with Moses and speak with him, relating to the concept of seeking the Lord at the tent of meeting
Moses gathers the elders at the tent of meeting where the Lord comes down, paralleling the tent of meeting outside the camp
The Lord calls Moses, Aaron, and Miriam out to the tent of meeting, showing the tent's function as a place of meeting with God
The Lord meets Moses at the tent of meeting, confirming the tent's role as the place for divine revelation
Describes how the Lord spoke with Moses face to face in this tent, expanding on verse 7
Refers to Jesus suffering outside the city gate, a typological parallel to the tent which was placed outside the camp
Thematic parallel about separation: The faithful group must physically move out or aside to meet God.
The tent as God's fixed point of communication: both for prophetic calling (leaders) and individual seeking (the people).
